rows.name: Air
rows.group: Elements of the quarters (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: Hebrew רוח Ruach; letter ו Vau of יהוה (777 col. LIV); world Yetzirah (col. LXIII); quarter-name מזרח Mezrach (col. LVII); Sphinx power Noscere, to know (col. L)
rows.note: The Golden Dawn places Air in the East. The Air-grade (Theoricus) opening faces East, and Raphael is set there in the Pentagram ritual.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) cols. L, LIV, LVII, LXIII; GD 2=9 Theoricus opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2, 1937)

rows.name: Fire
rows.group: Elements of the quarters (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: Hebrew אש Esh; letter י Yod; world Atziluth; quarter-name דרום Darom (777 col. LVII); Sphinx power Velle, to will (col. L)
rows.note: Fire belongs to the South, the quarter faced for the Fire-grade (Philosophus) invocation.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) cols. L, LIV, LVII, LXIII; GD 4=7 Philosophus opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2)

rows.name: Water
rows.group: Elements of the quarters (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: Hebrew מים Mayim; letter ה He; world Briah; quarter-name מערב Maareb (777 col. LVII); Sphinx power Audere, to dare (col. L)
rows.note: Water belongs to the West, the quarter faced for the Water-grade (Practicus) invocation.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) cols. L, LIV, LVII, LXIII; GD 3=8 Practicus opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2)

rows.name: Earth
rows.group: Elements of the quarters (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: Hebrew ארץ Aretz; final ה He; world Assiah; quarter-name צפון Tzaphon (777 col. LVII); Sphinx power Tacere, to keep silent (the conventional fourth power; the app's 777 col. L data has no entry for Earth)
rows.note: Earth belongs to the North, the quarter faced for the Earth-grade (Zelator) invocation before the Tablet of the North.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) cols. LIV, LVII, LXIII; GD 1=10 Zelator opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2)

rows.name: YHVH (Yod Heh Vau Heh)
rows.group: LBRP — divine names
rows.extra: יהוה; Liber O writes IHVH and gives the pronunciation 'Ye-ho-wau'; 1st pentagram
rows.note: In the Lesser Ritual the first pentagram is drawn in the East and charged by vibrating the Tetragrammaton.
rows.source: Crowley, Liber O vel Manus et Sagittae (Equinox I:2, 1909), Lesser Ritual of the Pentagram; GD First Knowledge Lecture (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 1, 1937)

rows.name: Adonai (ADNI)
rows.group: LBRP — divine names
rows.extra: אדני 'Lord'; 2nd pentagram (deosil circuit E→S→W→N)
rows.note: Moving on to the South, the operator draws the second pentagram and vibrates Adonai.
rows.source: Liber O (Equinox I:2, 1909), Lesser Ritual of the Pentagram; Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 1

rows.name: Eheieh (AHIH)
rows.group: LBRP — divine names
rows.extra: אהיה 'I am / I will be' (Exodus 3:14); 3rd pentagram
rows.note: In the West the third pentagram is charged with Eheieh.
rows.source: Liber O (Equinox I:2, 1909), Lesser Ritual of the Pentagram; Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 1

rows.name: AGLA
rows.group: LBRP — divine names
rows.extra: אגלא; notarikon of Atah Gibor Le-olam Adonai ('Thou art mighty for ever, O Lord'); 4th pentagram
rows.note: In the North the fourth pentagram is charged with AGLA, and then the operator returns to the East.
rows.source: Liber O (Equinox I:2, 1909), Lesser Ritual of the Pentagram; Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 1

rows.name: Raphael
rows.group: LBRP — archangels
rows.extra: רפאל 'God heals'; 'before me'; archangel of Air
rows.note: Standing facing East with arms in a cross, the operator names Raphael in front of him.
rows.source: Liber O (Equinox I:2, 1909), Lesser Ritual of the Pentagram; Liber 777 (1909) col. LIX 'Archangels of the Quarters'

rows.name: Michael
rows.group: LBRP — archangels
rows.extra: מיכאל 'Who is like God'; 'on my right hand'; archangel of Fire
rows.note: Michael is named at the right hand, which is South when facing East.
rows.source: Liber O (Equinox I:2, 1909); Liber 777 (1909) col. LIX

rows.name: Gabriel
rows.group: LBRP — archangels
rows.extra: גבריאל 'Strength of God'; 'behind me'; archangel of Water
rows.note: Gabriel is named behind the operator, in the West.
rows.source: Liber O (Equinox I:2, 1909); Liber 777 (1909) col. LIX

rows.name: Auriel (Uriel)
rows.group: LBRP — archangels
rows.extra: אוריאל 'Light of God'; 'on my left hand'; archangel of Earth; Liber O and 777 spell it Auriel
rows.note: Auriel is named at the left hand, which is North when facing East.
rows.source: Liber O (Equinox I:2, 1909); Liber 777 (1909) col. LIX

rows.name: Man — Aquarius
rows.group: Kerubic signs (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: ♒ 'sign of the head of the Man'; 777 col. XXXVIII (Air row) lists 'Eagle, Man (Cherub of Air)'
rows.note: The Air-grade opening invokes toward the East using the sign of the Man's head (Aquarius).
rows.source: GD 2=9 Theoricus opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2); Liber 777 (1909) col. XXXVIII

rows.name: Lion — Leo
rows.group: Kerubic signs (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: ♌ 'sign of the Lion'; 777 col. XXXVIII (Fire row): 'Lion (Cherub of Fire)'
rows.note: The Fire-grade invocation toward the South uses the sign of the Lion.
rows.source: GD 4=7 Philosophus opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2); Liber 777 (1909) col. XXXVIII

rows.name: Eagle — Scorpio
rows.group: Kerubic signs (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: ♏ 'sign of the Eagle'; 777 col. XXXVIII (Water row): 'Eagle-Snake-Scorpion (Cherub of Water)'
rows.note: The Water-grade invocation toward the West uses the sign of the Eagle.
rows.source: GD 3=8 Practicus opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2); Liber 777 (1909) col. XXXVIII

rows.name: Bull (Ox) — Taurus
rows.group: Kerubic signs (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: ♉ 'sign of the head of the Ox'; 777 col. XXXVIII (Taurus row): 'Bull (Cherub of Earth)'
rows.note: The Earth-grade invocation toward the North uses the sign of the Ox's head, together with the name of Auriel.
rows.source: GD 1=10 Zelator opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2); Liber 777 (1909) col. XXXVIII

rows.name: Dagger
rows.group: Elemental weapons (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: 777 col. XLI (Air row): 'The Dagger or Fan'
rows.note: In the Golden Dawn set of four elemental weapons, the Air Dagger belongs to the eastern quarter.
rows.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (Inner Order papers on the elemental weapons); Liber 777 (1909) col. XLI

rows.name: Wand
rows.group: Elemental weapons (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: 777 col. XLI (Fire row): 'The Wand or Lamp, Pyramid of Fire'
rows.note: The Fire Wand belongs to the southern quarter.
rows.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (elemental weapons); Liber 777 (1909) col. XLI

rows.name: Cup
rows.group: Elemental weapons (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: 777 col. XLI (Water row): 'The Cup and Cross of Suffering, the Wine'
rows.note: The Water Cup belongs to the western quarter.
rows.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (elemental weapons); Liber 777 (1909) col. XLI

rows.name: Pentacle
rows.group: Elemental weapons (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: Crowley spells it 'Pantacle' (Book 4 Part II, 1913)
rows.note: The Earth Pentacle belongs to the northern quarter.
rows.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (elemental weapons); Crowley, Book 4 Part II (1913)

rows.name: Eurus
rows.group: The four winds
rows.extra: Greek Εὖρος; Agrippa says it is also called Apeliotes; this is the wind's direction, not a GD element attribution
rows.note: Agrippa describes the east wind as damp, cloudy and devouring, and sets it against Zephyrus.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1533; J.F. trans. 1651), Bk I ch. 6 'Of the wonderful natures of Water, Air, and Winds'

rows.name: Notus
rows.group: The four winds
rows.extra: Greek Νότος; Latin Auster
rows.note: Agrippa's south wind is warm, wet, cloudy and unhealthy, and it brings the rains.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Bk I ch. 6

rows.name: Zephyrus
rows.group: The four winds
rows.extra: Greek Ζέφυρος; Latin Favonius
rows.note: Agrippa's west wind is the gentle one that ends winter and brings out leaves and flowers.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Bk I ch. 6

rows.name: Boreas
rows.group: The four winds
rows.extra: Greek Βορέας; Latin Aquilo
rows.note: Agrippa's north wind is violent: it drives off clouds, clears the sky and freezes water.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Bk I ch. 6

rows.name: Paralda
rows.group: Elemental kings (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: 777 col. LXII 'Kings of the Elemental Spirits'; the same names occur in Éliphas Lévi
rows.note: Paralda rules the spirits of Air, and so of the eastern quarter.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXII; cf. Lévi, Dogme et Rituel de la Haute Magie (1856)

rows.name: Djin
rows.group: Elemental kings (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: 777 col. LXII
rows.note: Djin rules the spirits of Fire in the southern quarter.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXII; cf. Lévi (1856)

rows.name: Niksa
rows.group: Elemental kings (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: 777 col. LXII; also spelled Nichsa or Nicksa
rows.note: Niksa rules the spirits of Water in the western quarter.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXII; cf. Lévi (1856)

rows.name: Ghob
rows.group: Elemental kings (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: 777 col. LXII; also spelled Gob
rows.note: Ghob rules the spirits of Earth in the northern quarter.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXII; cf. Lévi (1856)

rows.name: Sylphs
rows.group: Elemental beings
rows.extra: 777 col. CLXXXIII 'Legendary Orders of Being'
rows.note: Sylphs are Paracelsus's spirits of Air; through the Air–East attribution they belong to the East.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) cols. CLXXXIII and LVII; Paracelsus, Liber de nymphis, sylphis, pygmaeis et salamandris (1566)

rows.name: Salamanders
rows.group: Elemental beings
rows.extra: 777 col. CLXXXIII
rows.note: Salamanders are the spirits of Fire and belong to the South.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) cols. CLXXXIII and LVII; Paracelsus (1566)

rows.name: Undines
rows.group: Elemental beings
rows.extra: 777: 'Nymphs and Undines, Nereids, &c.'
rows.note: Undines and nymphs are the spirits of Water and belong to the West.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) cols. CLXXXIII and LVII; Paracelsus (1566)

rows.name: Gnomes
rows.group: Elemental beings
rows.extra: 777 col. CLXXXIII, listed with 'The Dweller of the Threshold'
rows.note: Gnomes (Paracelsus's pygmies) are the spirits of Earth and belong to the North.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) cols. CLXXXIII and LVII; Paracelsus (1566)

rows.name: Yellow / violet
rows.group: Flashing colours (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: Air tablet: yellow with violet letters; 777 King scale for Air: bright pale yellow (col. XV)
rows.note: Air is shown in yellow against its complement, violet, so that the colours seem to flash.
rows.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (Llewellyn 6th ed., 1989) p. 479, as cited in Wikipedia 'Watchtower (magic)'; Liber 777 col. XV

rows.name: Red / green
rows.group: Flashing colours (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: Fire tablet: red with green letters; 777 King scale for Fire: glowing orange scarlet
rows.note: Fire is shown in red against its complement, green.
rows.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (1989) p. 479, via Wikipedia 'Watchtower (magic)'; Liber 777 col. XV

rows.name: Blue / orange
rows.group: Flashing colours (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: Water tablet: blue with orange letters; 777 King scale for Water: deep blue
rows.note: Water is shown in blue against its complement, orange.
rows.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (1989) p. 479, via Wikipedia 'Watchtower (magic)'; Liber 777 col. XV

rows.name: Black / green (variants)
rows.group: Flashing colours (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: variants: black/white, or 777 col. XV for Earth: 'Citrine, russet, olive & black (quartered)'
rows.note: Wikipedia's reading of Regardie gives the Earth tablet as black with green letters, but sources differ and black has no true complementary colour.
rows.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn (1989) p. 479, via Wikipedia 'Watchtower (magic)'; Liber 777 col. XV

rows.name: Ariel
rows.group: Rulers of the elements (777)
rows.extra: אריאל
rows.note: Liber 777 makes Ariel the ruler of Air, and so of the eastern quarter; Agrippa gives Ariel to Earth instead.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LX 'The Rulers of the Elements'

rows.name: Seraph
rows.group: Rulers of the elements (777)
rows.extra: שרף
rows.note: Seraph rules Fire in the South.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LX

rows.name: Tharsis
rows.group: Rulers of the elements (777)
rows.extra: תרשיס
rows.note: Tharsis rules Water in the West.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LX

rows.name: Kerub
rows.group: Rulers of the elements (777)
rows.extra: כרוב
rows.note: Kerub rules Earth in the North; Agrippa gives Cherub to Air instead.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LX

rows.name: Chassan
rows.group: Angels of the elements (777)
rows.extra: חסן
rows.note: Liber 777 makes Chassan the angel of Air.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXI 'Angels of the Elements'

rows.name: Aral
rows.group: Angels of the elements (777)
rows.extra: אראל
rows.note: Liber 777 makes Aral the angel of Fire.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXI

rows.name: Taliahad
rows.group: Angels of the elements (777)
rows.extra: printed תליהד in 777 (GD spelling טליהד)
rows.note: Liber 777 makes Taliahad the angel of Water.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXI

rows.name: Phorlakh
rows.group: Angels of the elements (777)
rows.extra: פורלאך
rows.note: Liber 777 makes Phorlakh the angel of Earth.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. LXI

rows.name: Shaddai El Chai
rows.group: Elemental grade divine names (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: שדי אל חי 'Almighty Living God'; Theoricus 2=9
rows.note: The Air-grade opening faces East and invokes under this name, with Raphael as archangel.
rows.source: GD 2=9 Theoricus opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2, 1937)

rows.name: YHVH Tzabaoth
rows.group: Elemental grade divine names (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: יהוה צבאות 'Lord of Hosts' (the ritual says 'Tetragrammaton Tzabaoth'); Philosophus 4=7
rows.note: The Fire-grade opening faces South and invokes under this name, with Michael as archangel.
rows.source: GD 4=7 Philosophus opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2)

rows.name: Elohim Tzabaoth
rows.group: Elemental grade divine names (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: אלהים צבאות 'God of Hosts'; Practicus 3=8
rows.note: The Water-grade opening faces West and invokes under this name, with Gabriel as archangel.
rows.source: GD 3=8 Practicus opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2)

rows.name: Adonai ha-Aretz / Adonai Melekh
rows.group: Elemental grade divine names (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: אדני הארץ 'Lord of the Earth', אדני מלך 'Lord and King'; Adonai Melekh is the name used in the actual invocation; Zelator 1=10
rows.note: The Earth-grade opening faces North, adores under Adonai ha-Aretz and Adonai Melekh, and invokes with Auriel as archangel.
rows.source: GD 1=10 Zelator opening (Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2)

rows.name: Tablet of Air (EXARP)
rows.group: Enochian Watchtowers (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: EXARP is its line of the Tablet of Union; three holy names ORO IBAH AOZPI; Great King BATAIVAH ('Great King of the East' in the 2=9)
rows.note: The Golden Dawn sets Dee's Air tablet in the East, and its names are invoked in the Theoricus opening.
rows.source: GD 2=9 Theoricus opening; Regardie, The Golden Dawn (Enochian papers, SIRP); Crowley, Liber Chanokh (Equinox I:7–8, 1912)

rows.name: Tablet of Fire (BITOM)
rows.group: Enochian Watchtowers (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: three holy names OIP TEAA PEDOCE (OIP TEAA PDOCE); Great King EDLPRNAA ('Edelperna, Great King of the South' in the 4=7)
rows.note: The Fire tablet is set in the South, and its names are invoked in the Philosophus opening.
rows.source: GD 4=7 Philosophus opening; Regardie, The Golden Dawn; Liber Chanokh (1912)

rows.name: Tablet of Water (HCOMA)
rows.group: Enochian Watchtowers (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: three holy names EMPEH ARSEL GAIOL (MPH ARSL GAIOL); Great King RAAGIOSL ('Ra-agiosel, Great King of the West' in the 3=8)
rows.note: The Water tablet is set in the West, and its names are invoked in the Practicus opening.
rows.source: GD 3=8 Practicus opening; Regardie, The Golden Dawn; Liber Chanokh (1912)

rows.name: Tablet of Earth (NANTA)
rows.group: Enochian Watchtowers (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: three holy names EMOR DIAL HECTEGA (MOR DIAL HCTGA); Great King ICZHIHAL ('Ic Zod Heh Chal, Great King of the North' in the 1=10)
rows.note: The Earth tablet is set in the North, and its names are invoked in the Zelator opening.
rows.source: GD 1=10 Zelator opening; Regardie, The Golden Dawn; Liber Chanokh (1912)

rows.name: YHVH (Air pentagram)
rows.role: divine name of the elemental pentagram
rows.group: Supreme Ritual of the Pentagram (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: active Spirit pentagram: EXARP + Eheieh אהיה; then Air pentagram: ORO IBAH AOZPI + YHVH; sign of Aquarius
rows.note: In the Supreme ritual the East gets an active Spirit pentagram and then an Air pentagram charged with YHVH.
rows.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn, 'Supreme Invoking Ritual of the Pentagram' (Inner Order material as arranged by Regardie)

rows.name: Elohim (Fire pentagram)
rows.role: divine name of the elemental pentagram
rows.group: Supreme Ritual of the Pentagram (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: active Spirit pentagram: BITOM + Eheieh; then Fire pentagram: OIP TEAA PEDOCE + אלהים Elohim; sign of Leo
rows.note: The South gets an active Spirit pentagram and then a Fire pentagram charged with Elohim.
rows.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn, 'Supreme Invoking Ritual of the Pentagram'

rows.name: El (Water pentagram)
rows.role: divine name of the elemental pentagram
rows.group: Supreme Ritual of the Pentagram (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: passive Spirit pentagram: HCOMA + AGLA אגלא; then Water pentagram: EMPEH ARSEL GAIOL + אל El; eagle's-head sign
rows.note: The West gets a passive Spirit pentagram and then a Water pentagram charged with El.
rows.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn, 'Supreme Invoking Ritual of the Pentagram'

rows.name: Adonai (Earth pentagram)
rows.role: divine name of the elemental pentagram
rows.group: Supreme Ritual of the Pentagram (Golden Dawn)
rows.extra: passive Spirit pentagram: NANTA + AGLA; then Earth pentagram: EMOR DIAL HECTEGA + אדני Adonai (some versions Adonai ha-Aretz); sign of Taurus
rows.note: The North gets a passive Spirit pentagram and then an Earth pentagram charged with Adonai.
rows.source: Regardie, The Golden Dawn, 'Supreme Invoking Ritual of the Pentagram'

rows.name: Hexagram of Fire
rows.group: Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram (Liber O)
rows.extra: ARARITA is said; an elemental form, not a planet (zodiacal quarters: Aries East)
rows.note: Liber O traces the Fire form of the hexagram in the East, so the hexagram's quarters differ from the pentagram's.
rows.source: Crowley, Liber O vel Manus et Sagittae (Equinox I:2, 1909), Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram

rows.name: Hexagram of Earth
rows.group: Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram (Liber O)
rows.extra: ARARITA
rows.note: The Earth form of the hexagram is traced in the South.
rows.source: Liber O (Equinox I:2, 1909), Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram

rows.name: Hexagram of Air
rows.group: Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram (Liber O)
rows.extra: ARARITA
rows.note: The Air form of the hexagram is traced in the West.
rows.source: Liber O (Equinox I:2, 1909), Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram

rows.name: Hexagram of Water
rows.group: Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram (Liber O)
rows.extra: ARARITA
rows.note: The Water form of the hexagram is traced in the North.
rows.source: Liber O (Equinox I:2, 1909), Lesser Ritual of the Hexagram

rows.name: Hierophant
rows.group: Neophyte Hall stations (GD 0=0)
rows.extra: Throne of the East; the rising of the Sun of Life and Light
rows.note: The Hierophant rules from the Throne of the East, which stands for the rising of the Sun of Life and Light.
rows.source: GD 0=0 Neophyte ritual, opening (printed in The Equinox I:2, 1909; Regardie, The Golden Dawn vol. 2)

rows.name: Dadouchos
rows.group: Neophyte Hall stations (GD 0=0)
rows.extra: torch-bearer; censer, purification by Fire; heat and dryness
rows.note: The Dadouchos stands in the South, standing for heat and dryness, and purifies with fire.
rows.source: GD 0=0 Neophyte ritual, opening (Equinox I:2, 1909; Regardie vol. 2)

rows.name: Hiereus
rows.group: Neophyte Hall stations (GD 0=0)
rows.extra: Throne of the West; increase of darkness, decrease of light
rows.note: The Hiereus sits on the Throne of the West, the place where darkness grows and light wanes.
rows.source: GD 0=0 Neophyte ritual, opening (Equinox I:2, 1909; Regardie vol. 2)

rows.name: Stolistes
rows.group: Neophyte Hall stations (GD 0=0)
rows.extra: cup of lustral water, purification by Water; cold and moisture; the North is 'the place of greatest symbolic darkness'
rows.note: The Stolistes stands in the North, standing for cold and moisture. After the obligation the candidate is led to the North, the darkest part of the Hall.
rows.source: GD 0=0 Neophyte ritual (Equinox I:2, 1909; Regardie vol. 2)

rows.name: Michael
rows.role: angel ruling a corner of the world
rows.group: Agrippa — Scale of the Number Four (variant)
rows.extra: same column: Fire; ruler Seraph; animal Lion
rows.note: Agrippa's table puts Michael in the same column as the East and Fire, whereas the Golden Dawn gives Michael the South.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1533; J.F. trans. 1651), Bk II ch. 7, Scale of the Number Four

rows.name: Uriel
rows.role: angel ruling a corner of the world
rows.group: Agrippa — Scale of the Number Four (variant)
rows.extra: same column: Earth (עפר); ruler Ariel; animal Calf
rows.note: Agrippa puts Uriel in the same column as the South and Earth.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Bk II ch. 7

rows.name: Raphael
rows.role: angel ruling a corner of the world
rows.group: Agrippa — Scale of the Number Four (variant)
rows.extra: same column: Air; ruler Cherub; animal Eagle
rows.note: Agrippa puts Raphael in the same column as the West and Air.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Bk II ch. 7

rows.name: Gabriel
rows.role: angel ruling a corner of the world
rows.group: Agrippa — Scale of the Number Four (variant)
rows.extra: same column: Water; ruler Tharsis; animal Man
rows.note: Agrippa puts Gabriel in the same column as the North and Water.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Bk II ch. 7

rows.name: Tiphareth
rows.group: Sepher Yetzirah directions (777 col. CX)
rows.extra: תפארת; in the same column Chesed = Height and Geburah = Depth
rows.note: Liber 777 maps the six sealed directions of the Sepher Yetzirah onto Sephiroth 4–9, which gives the East to Tiphareth.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. CX 'Elements and Quarters (Sepher Yetzirah)', after Sepher Yetzirah 1:13

rows.name: Hod
rows.group: Sepher Yetzirah directions (777 col. CX)
rows.extra: הוד
rows.note: In the same table, Hod is the South.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. CX

rows.name: Netzach
rows.group: Sepher Yetzirah directions (777 col. CX)
rows.extra: נצח
rows.note: In the same table, Netzach is the West.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. CX

rows.name: Yesod
rows.group: Sepher Yetzirah directions (777 col. CX)
rows.extra: יסוד
rows.note: In the same table, Yesod is the North.
rows.source: Liber 777 (1909) col. CX

rows.name: Ra
rows.group: Liber Resh vel Helios
rows.extra: sunrise; Ra 'in Thy rising' and 'in Thy strength'; the Sun's bark comes 'from the Abodes of Night'
rows.note: At dawn the aspirant faces East, gives the sign of his grade and hails the Sun as Ra.
rows.source: Crowley, Liber Resh vel Helios sub figura CC §1 (The Equinox I:6, 1911)

rows.name: Ahathoor
rows.group: Liber Resh vel Helios
rows.extra: noon; 'in Thy triumphing' and 'in Thy beauty'; 'from the Abodes of Morning'
rows.note: At noon the aspirant faces South and hails the Sun as Ahathoor (Hathor).
rows.source: Liber Resh vel Helios §2 (Equinox I:6, 1911)

rows.name: Tum
rows.group: Liber Resh vel Helios
rows.extra: sunset; 'in Thy setting' and 'in Thy joy'; 'from the Abodes of Day'
rows.note: At sunset the aspirant faces West and hails the Sun as Tum (Atum).
rows.source: Liber Resh vel Helios §3 (Equinox I:6, 1911)

rows.name: Khephra
rows.group: Liber Resh vel Helios
rows.extra: midnight; 'in Thy hiding' and 'in Thy silence'; 'from the Abodes of Evening'; the app's data/resh.json spells it 'Khepra'
rows.note: At midnight the aspirant faces North and hails the hidden Sun as Khephra (Khepri).
rows.source: Liber Resh vel Helios §4 (Equinox I:6, 1911)

rows.name: ΧΑΟΣ (Chaos)
rows.group: Star Ruby — 1913 (Book of Lies)
rows.extra: roared; 1st station; the circuit is widdershins E→N→W→S
rows.note: Advancing to the East, the operator projects the pentagram with the sign of Horus and roars Chaos.
rows.source: Crowley, The Book of Lies (Wieland, 1913), ch. 25 (ΚΕ) 'The Star Ruby'

rows.name: ΒΑΒΑΛΟΝ (Babalon)
rows.group: Star Ruby — 1913 (Book of Lies)
rows.extra: screamed; 2nd station
rows.note: Going widdershins to the North, the operator repeats the gesture and screams Babalon.
rows.source: The Book of Lies (1913), ch. 25

rows.name: ΕΡΩΣ (Eros)
rows.group: Star Ruby — 1913 (Book of Lies)
rows.extra: said; 3rd station
rows.note: In the West the gesture is repeated and Eros is spoken.
rows.source: The Book of Lies (1913), ch. 25

rows.name: ΨΥΧΗ (Psyche)
rows.group: Star Ruby — 1913 (Book of Lies)
rows.extra: bellowed; 4th station
rows.note: In the South the operator bellows Psyche, then completes the circle and returns to the centre.
rows.source: The Book of Lies (1913), ch. 25

rows.name: ΘΗΡΙΟΝ (Therion)
rows.group: Star Ruby — 1929 revision (MTP)
rows.extra: roared; replaces ΧΑΟΣ; the only one of the four new names printed in Greek; widdershins circuit
rows.note: In the revised rite the East pentagram is charged with Therion, the Beast.
rows.source: Crowley, Magick in Theory and Practice (Paris: Lecram, 1929), Appendix VI, Liber XXV

rows.name: NUIT
rows.group: Star Ruby — 1929 revision (MTP)
rows.extra: said; replaces ΒΑΒΑΛΟΝ; printed in Roman capitals
rows.note: In the revision the North takes Nuit, and Babalon moves to the West.
rows.source: Magick in Theory and Practice (1929), App. VI, Liber XXV (collated in the O.T.O./Celephaïs e-text footnotes)

rows.name: BABALON
rows.group: Star Ruby — 1929 revision (MTP)
rows.extra: whispered; replaces ΕΡΩΣ
rows.note: In the revision the West takes Babalon, whispered.
rows.source: Magick in Theory and Practice (1929), App. VI, Liber XXV

rows.name: HADIT
rows.group: Star Ruby — 1929 revision (MTP)
rows.extra: bellowed; replaces ΨΥΧΗ
rows.note: In the revision the South takes Hadit, bellowed.
rows.source: Magick in Theory and Practice (1929), App. VI, Liber XXV

rows.name: Iynges (ΙΥΓΓΕΣ)
rows.group: Star Ruby — guardians (both versions)
rows.extra: ΠΡΟ ΜΟΥ ΙΥΓΓΕΣ
rows.note: Standing in the centre with arms in a Tau, the operator places the Iynges in front of him. That is East if he faces East there, as he does at the start and end of the rite.
rows.source: The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 25; MTP (1929) App. VI; the terms come from the Chaldean Oracles

rows.name: Teletarchae (ΤΕΛΕΤΑΡΧΑΙ)
rows.group: Star Ruby — guardians (both versions)
rows.extra: ΟΠΙΣΩ ΜΟΥ ΤΕΛΕΤΑΡΧΑΙ
rows.note: The Teletarchs are placed behind the operator, which is West when facing East.
rows.source: The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 25; MTP (1929) App. VI

rows.name: Synoches (ΣΥΝΟΧΕΣ)
rows.role: Chaldean-Oracle power — on my right hand
rows.group: Star Ruby — guardians (both versions)
rows.extra: ΕΠΙ ΔΕΞΙΑ ΣΥΝΟΧΕΣ
rows.note: The Synoches are at the right hand, which is South when facing East.
rows.source: The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 25; MTP (1929) App. VI

rows.name: Daimones (ΔΑΙΜΟΝΕΣ)
rows.group: Star Ruby — guardians (both versions)
rows.extra: ΕΠΑΡΙΣΤΕΡΑ ΔΑΙΜΟΝΕΣ
rows.note: The daimons are at the left hand, which is North when facing East.
rows.source: The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 25; MTP (1929) App. VI

rows.name: Boleskine — facing
rows.group: Liber V vel Reguli
rows.note: The Magician begins by turning to face Boleskine, which the text calls the House of the Beast 666, and projects the force radiating from it as he circles.
rows.source: Crowley, Liber V vel Reguli, First Gesture (Magick in Theory and Practice, 1929, App. VI); coordinates from OS NGR NH 50847 22116 (Buildings at Risk Register) converted to WGS84

rows.name: Nuit
rows.group: Liber V vel Reguli
rows.extra: averse pentagram invoking Air (Aquarius); sign Puella; 1st station, reached by turning to the left (widdershins)
rows.note: In the Enchantment the Magician halts in the North, traces the averse Air pentagram and calls on Nuit.
rows.source: Liber V vel Reguli, Second Gesture 'The Enchantment' (MTP 1929, App. VI)

rows.name: Hadit
rows.group: Liber V vel Reguli
rows.extra: averse pentagram invoking Fire (Leo); sign Puer; 2nd station
rows.note: Halting next in the South, he traces the averse Fire pentagram and cries Hadit.
rows.source: Liber V vel Reguli, Second Gesture (MTP 1929, App. VI)

rows.name: Therion
rows.group: Liber V vel Reguli
rows.extra: averse pentagram invoking Earth (Taurus); sign Vir; 3rd station
rows.note: In the East he traces the averse Earth pentagram and cries Therion.
rows.source: Liber V vel Reguli, Second Gesture (MTP 1929, App. VI)

rows.name: Babalon
rows.group: Liber V vel Reguli
rows.extra: averse pentagram invoking Water (no zodiac sign named); sign Mulier; 4th station
rows.note: In the West he traces the averse Water pentagram and calls on Babalon.
rows.source: Liber V vel Reguli, Second Gesture (MTP 1929, App. VI)

rows.name: Boleskine House (Temple East / High Altar)
rows.group: Liber XV — Gnostic Mass
rows.note: Liber XV defines the temple's East as the direction of Boleskine, on the south-eastern shore of Loch Ness two miles east of Foyers. The High Altar stands there, the small altar and font are in the middle, and the Tomb is at the West end.
rows.source: Crowley, Liber XV, Ecclesiae Gnosticae Catholicae Canon Missae §I (The International, 1918; Equinox III:1, 1919); coordinates from OS NGR NH 50847 22116 converted to WGS84 (Wikipedia gives 57.2653°N 4.4747°W)

rows.name: Section B — Air
rows.group: Liber Samekh (Point II notes)
rows.extra: opening barbarous names AR ThIAF RhEIBET…; golden light; from here the Adept circles widdershins (astrally)
rows.note: Crowley's explanation of the ritual has the Adept invoke Air in the East, sending out a shaft of golden light.
rows.source: Crowley, Liber Samekh, Point II explanatory notes, Magick in Theory and Practice (1929), Appendix IV

rows.name: Section C — Fire
rows.group: Liber Samekh (Point II notes)
rows.extra: opening names AR-O-GO-GO-RU-ABRAO SOTOU…; flame-red rays
rows.note: The Adept next invokes Fire in the South, with red flame streaming from him.
rows.source: Liber Samekh, Point II notes (MTP 1929, App. IV)

rows.name: Section D — Water
rows.group: Liber Samekh (Point II notes)
rows.extra: opening names RU-ABRA-IAF MRIODOM…; blue radiance
rows.note: He invokes Water in the West, and his wand pours out blue light.
rows.source: Liber Samekh, Point II notes (MTP 1929, App. IV)

rows.name: Section E — Earth
rows.group: Liber Samekh (Point II notes)
rows.extra: opening names MA BARRAIO IOEL…; green flame
rows.note: He goes to the North to invoke Earth, with green fire flashing from his weapon.
rows.source: Liber Samekh, Point II notes (MTP 1929, App. IV)

rows.name: Section F — Spirit (toward Boleskine)
rows.group: Liber Samekh (Point II notes)
rows.extra: 57.2653,-4.4748; active pentagrams, the Mark of the Beast and the L.V.X. signs; opening names AFT ABAFT BAS-AUMGN…
rows.note: For Spirit, the Adept goes back to the centre and invokes facing Boleskine, using the active pentagrams and the Mark of the Beast.
rows.source: Liber Samekh, Point II notes (MTP 1929, App. IV)

rows.name: Pater et Mater unus deus Ararita
rows.group: Star Sapphire (Liber XXXVI)
rows.extra: Holy Hexagram; 1st station; deosil circuit E→S→W→N; the 1913 text prints 'UNIS' at this station
rows.note: From the centre the adept goes to the East, makes the Holy Hexagram and proclaims Father and Mother as one god, Ararita.
rows.source: Crowley, The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 36 'The Star Sapphire'; reprinted in MTP (1929) App. VI

rows.name: Mater et Filius unus deus Ararita
rows.group: Star Sapphire (Liber XXXVI)
rows.extra: Holy Hexagram; 2nd station
rows.note: In the South the hexagram is made with the formula of Mother and Son.
rows.source: The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 36; MTP (1929) App. VI

rows.name: Filius et Filia unus deus Ararita
rows.group: Star Sapphire (Liber XXXVI)
rows.extra: Holy Hexagram; 3rd station
rows.note: In the West the hexagram is made with the formula of Son and Daughter.
rows.source: The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 36; MTP (1929) App. VI

rows.name: Filia et Pater unus deus Ararita
rows.group: Star Sapphire (Liber XXXVI)
rows.extra: Holy Hexagram; 4th station
rows.note: In the North the hexagram is made with the formula of Daughter and Father, and then the adept returns to the centre.
rows.source: The Book of Lies (1913) ch. 36; MTP (1929) App. VI

rows.name: Amaymon
rows.role: king of the East (first of the four great kings)
rows.group: Four Kings of the quarters — Goetia 1904
rows.extra: 1904 print spellings: AMAYMON (Observations p. 31; spirits 13, 32, 33, 70) and AMAIMON (Invocation of the King p. 43; Enochian 'Potent Invocatioun of Hys Kynge' p. 59). Spirits named as his: 32 Asmoday, 33 Gäap, 70 Seere.
rows.note: First of the four great kings over the 72, and the only one whose quarter the text states outright. The Invocation of the King addresses him as ruler in the Dominion of the East, and Seere's entry calls him King of the East. The kings are invoked to send their spirits and are called forth themselves only on great occasions.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904): Observations p. 31; The Invocation of the King p. 43 and its footnote; Ye Potent Invocatioun of Hys Kynge p. 59; spirit 70 (checked against the scan of the 1904 printing on Wikimedia Commons)

rows.name: Corson
rows.role: king (one of the four great kings)
rows.group: Four Kings of the quarters — Goetia 1904
rows.extra: 1904 print p. 31: CORSON. Weyer/Scot: Gorson, King of the SOUTH. Crowley's footnote on p. 59 of the same edition names Paimon, not Corson, for the West. Not the same as spirit 20 Purson.
rows.note: Second of the four kings in the list, which the text follows with 'East, West, North, and South'. West comes only from reading the two lists in order.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), Observations p. 31

rows.name: Ziminiar (Zimimay)
rows.role: king (one of the four great kings)
rows.group: Four Kings of the quarters — Goetia 1904
rows.extra: 1904 print p. 31: ZIMIMAY or ZIMINIAR; p. 59 footnote: Zodimay (North by order). de Laurence 1916: ZIMIMAY or ZIMINAIR. Weyer: Zymymar. Scot: Zimimar.
rows.note: Third of the four kings. Reading the lists in order makes him King of the North, and both Weyer and Crowley's Zodimay footnote agree.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), Observations p. 31 and footnote p. 59; cf. Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577), closing section

rows.name: Göap
rows.role: king (one of the four great kings)
rows.group: Four Kings of the quarters — Goetia 1904
rows.extra: 1904 print p. 31: GÖAP (the 2003 Celephaïs re-set prints GOAP). Crowley's p. 59 footnote puts 'Gaap' in the South position. Weyer: Goap, king and prince of the WEST. In the Observations he is distinct from spirit 33 Gäap.
rows.note: Fourth of the four kings. South comes from reading the lists in order, and Crowley's Enochian invocation in the same edition also pairs a 'Gaap' with the South. Weyer, the older source of this passage, makes Goap king of the West.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), Observations p. 31; Ye Potent Invocatioun of Hys Kynge, footnote p. 59

rows.name: Amaimon
rows.role: king of the East (default king of the invocation)
rows.group: Four Kings — Crowley's Enochian invocation (Goetia 1904 p. 59)
rows.extra: The English line reads 'kingdoms of the East' followed by '(South, West, North)' in brackets. Footnote on his name: Gaap, Paimon, Zodimay.
rows.note: Crowley's Angelic-language version of the Invocation of the King addresses Amaimon as ruling in the kingdoms of the East, with the other three quarters in brackets as alternatives.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), 'Ye Potent Invocatioun of Hys Kynge', p. 59 (1904 print scan, Wikimedia Commons)

rows.name: Gaap
rows.role: king invoked for the South (alternative to Amaimon)
rows.group: Four Kings — Crowley's Enochian invocation (Goetia 1904 p. 59)
rows.extra: Footnote: 'Or Gaap, Paimon, Zodimay, as the case may be.' Gaap stands where the Observations list GÖAP; spirit 33 is spelled Gäap.
rows.note: The footnote gives three substitutes for Amaimon in the same order as the bracketed South, West and North, which pairs Gaap with the South.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), footnote to 'Ye Potent Invocatioun of Hys Kynge', p. 59

rows.name: Paimon
rows.role: king invoked for the West (alternative to Amaimon)
rows.group: Four Kings — Crowley's Enochian invocation (Goetia 1904 p. 59)
rows.extra: Agrees with spirit 9 (observed towards the West) and with Agrippa, Oberon and Sloane 3853. Replaces Corson of the Observations.
rows.note: Paimon is the second substitute in the footnote, matched by order to the West.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), footnote p. 59

rows.name: Zodimay
rows.role: king invoked for the North (alternative to Amaimon)
rows.group: Four Kings — Crowley's Enochian invocation (Goetia 1904 p. 59)
rows.extra: The same king as the Observations' Zimimay/Ziminiar.
rows.note: Zodimay is the third substitute in the footnote, matched by order to the North.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), footnote p. 59

rows.name: Bael
rows.group: Goetia 1904 — spirits with a stated quarter
rows.extra: spirit 1. Weyer/Scot: 'of the power of the east'.
rows.note: The first principal spirit, a king ruling in the East.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), spirit 1

rows.name: Agares
rows.group: Goetia 1904 — spirits with a stated quarter
rows.extra: spirit 2; variant Agreas. Weyer/Scot: first duke under the power of the east.
rows.note: A duke under the power of the East.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), spirit 2

rows.name: Paimon
rows.group: Goetia 1904 — spirits with a stated quarter
rows.extra: spirit 9. Weyer: faces Aquilo (north); Scot: 'northwest'. Crowley's 1904 footnote (p. 59) also makes Paimon the king for the West.
rows.note: The text says he is to be observed towards the West. Weyer has the exorcist face north instead.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), spirit 9

rows.name: Beleth
rows.role: king (ritual gesture towards South and East)
rows.group: Goetia 1904 — spirits with a stated quarter
rows.extra: spirit 13. Weyer/Scot (Byleth): the rod is held toward the east and south. The silver ring is held to the face 'as before AMAYMON'.
rows.note: To handle him, the exorcist strikes a hazel wand out towards the South and East quarters and draws a triangle outside the circle. The point is plotted at the south-east midpoint.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), spirit 13

rows.name: Asmoday
rows.group: Goetia 1904 — spirits with a stated quarter
rows.extra: spirit 32. His 72 legions are counted among Amaymon's. In Oberon, Asmoday heads Amaymon's twelve, but there Amaymon is King of the South.
rows.note: First and choicest under the power of Amaymon, going before all the others. East is derived from Amaymon's stated quarter, since the entry itself names no direction.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), spirit 32

rows.name: Gäap
rows.group: Goetia 1904 — spirits with a stated quarter
rows.extra: spirit 33. Appears 'when the Sun is in some of the Southern Signs', which is zodiacal and not a compass point. Crowley's 1904 footnote (p. 59) names a 'Gaap' as the king for the SOUTH.
rows.note: He teaches how to consecrate things of the dominion of Amaymon, whom the text calls his King, so East is derived from that. The same edition's Enochian-invocation footnote treats Gaap as the southern king, so the two readings conflict.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), spirit 33; footnote p. 59

rows.name: Seere
rows.role: prince under Amaymon, King of the East
rows.group: Goetia 1904 — spirits with a stated quarter
rows.extra: spirit 70; variants Sear, Seir. Not in Weyer. Checked against the 1904 print (lesserkey.json crowley field).
rows.note: A mighty prince under Amaymon, whom this entry explicitly calls King of the East.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, Goetia (1904), spirit 70

rows.name: Amoymon (Amaymon)
rows.group: Variant kings — Pseudomonarchia daemonum (Weyer 1577 / Scot 1584)
rows.extra: Scot: Amaymon king of the east
rows.note: The closing section on binding hours names him King of the East. The four kings may be bound from the third hour until noon and from the ninth hour until evening.
rows.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (appendix to De praestigiis daemonum, 1577), closing section; Scot, Discoverie of Witchcraft (1584) XV.3

rows.name: Gorson
rows.group: Variant kings — Pseudomonarchia daemonum (Weyer 1577 / Scot 1584)
rows.extra: Goetia form: Corson
rows.note: King of the South in Weyer's list, where the Goetia's list order puts Corson in the West.
rows.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577), closing section; Scot (1584) XV.3

rows.name: Zymymar (Zimimar)
rows.group: Variant kings — Pseudomonarchia daemonum (Weyer 1577 / Scot 1584)
rows.extra: Scot: Zimimar; Goetia: Zimimay/Ziminiar
rows.note: King of the North, which agrees with the Goetia.
rows.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577), closing section; Scot (1584) XV.3

rows.name: Goap
rows.role: king and prince of the West
rows.group: Variant kings — Pseudomonarchia daemonum (Weyer 1577 / Scot 1584)
rows.extra: Goetia 1904: GÖAP (South by list order)
rows.note: King and prince of the West in Weyer, where the Goetia's list order puts Göap in the South.
rows.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577), closing section; Scot (1584) XV.3

rows.name: Baël
rows.group: Pseudomonarchia daemonum — spirits with a stated quarter
rows.extra: Weyer §1; = Goetia spirit 1
rows.note: The first king, of the power of the East.
rows.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577) §1; Scot (1584) XV.2

rows.name: Agares
rows.group: Pseudomonarchia daemonum — spirits with a stated quarter
rows.extra: Weyer §2; = Goetia spirit 2
rows.note: The first duke under the power of the East.
rows.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577) §2; Scot (1584) XV.2

rows.name: Byleth
rows.role: king (ritual gesture towards East and South)
rows.group: Pseudomonarchia daemonum — spirits with a stated quarter
rows.extra: Weyer §20; = Goetia spirit 13 Beleth
rows.note: The exorcist reaches a hazel rod out towards the East and South and makes a triangle beside the circle. The point is plotted at the south-east midpoint.
rows.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577) §20; Scot (1584) XV.2

rows.name: Paymon
rows.group: Pseudomonarchia daemonum — spirits with a stated quarter
rows.extra: Weyer §22. Latin 'Aquilonem versus' (Aquilo = the north wind); Scot's English: 'northwest'; Goetia spirit 9 says West.
rows.note: When calling him, the exorcist looks towards Aquilo, the north wind, because his dwelling is there.
rows.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577) §22; Scot (1584) XV.2

rows.name: Sydonay alias Asmoday
rows.group: Pseudomonarchia daemonum — spirits with a stated quarter
rows.extra: Weyer §35; = Goetia spirit 32
rows.note: He goes before the others who are under Amaymon's power. East is derived from Amaymon's quarter in Weyer.
rows.source: Weyer, Pseudomonarchia daemonum (1577) §35; Scot (1584) XV.2

rows.name: Urieus (Oriens)
rows.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
rows.extra: III.24 spelling: Urieus. II.7 'Scale of the number four': Oriens, in the same column as Fire and 'The East'.
rows.note: One of four most mischievous kings set over the four parts of the world. Agrippa names him King of the East, and his table of fours puts Oriens in the East column.
rows.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) III ch. 24 and II ch. 7; Eng. tr. J. F[reake] 1651

rows.name: Amaymon
rows.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
rows.extra: In both III.24 and the II.7 table (Earth / South column). Contradicts the Goetia and Weyer, which put him in the East.
rows.note: Agrippa makes Amaymon King of the South in both places.
rows.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) III ch. 24 and II ch. 7; Eng. tr. 1651

rows.name: Paymon
rows.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
rows.extra: In III.24 and the II.7 table (Air / West column). Agrees with Goetia spirit 9.
rows.note: Agrippa makes Paymon King of the West.
rows.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) III ch. 24 and II ch. 7; Eng. tr. 1651

rows.name: Egin (Egyn)
rows.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
rows.extra: III.24: Egin; II.7 table: Egyn (Water / North column). Mathers' 1904 footnote equates Egyn with Ariton.
rows.note: Agrippa makes Egin King of the North.
rows.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) III ch. 24 and II ch. 7; Eng. tr. 1651

rows.name: Samael (Samuel)
rows.role: Hebrew name for the king of the East; prince of devils (Fire)
rows.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
rows.extra: III.24 (1651): 'Samuel'; II.7 table: Samael, in the Fire / East column. Both placements give East.
rows.note: Agrippa gives the Hebrew doctors' names for the four kings with a hedge ('perhaps'). Samael falls in the East whether the names are matched by list order (III.24) or by the table's columns (II.7).
rows.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) II ch. 7 (Scale of Four) and III ch. 24; Eng. tr. 1651

rows.name: Azazel
rows.role: prince of devils (Air); Hebrew name of a quarter-king
rows.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
rows.extra: II.7 table: Azazel in the Air / West column, under Paymon. III.24 list order would give SOUTH (matched to Amaymon).
rows.note: In Agrippa's table of fours Azazel stands in the West column with Paymon. The order of the III.24 list would instead pair him with Amaymon in the South.
rows.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) II ch. 7 (Scale of Four); cf. III ch. 24; Eng. tr. 1651

rows.name: Azael
rows.role: prince of devils (Water); Hebrew name of a quarter-king
rows.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
rows.extra: II.7 table: Azael in the Water / North column, under Egyn. III.24 list order would give WEST (matched to Paymon).
rows.note: In the table of fours Azael shares the North column with Egyn. The III.24 order would pair him with Paymon in the West.
rows.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) II ch. 7 (Scale of Four); cf. III ch. 24; Eng. tr. 1651

rows.name: Mahazael (Mahazuel)
rows.role: prince of devils (Earth); Hebrew name of a quarter-king
rows.group: Variant kings — Agrippa, Occult Philosophy II.7 & III.24
rows.extra: III.24 (1651): 'Mahazuel'. II.7 table: Mahazael in the Earth / South column, under Amaymon. III.24 list order would give NORTH (matched to Egin).
rows.note: In the table of fours Mahazael shares the South column with Amaymon. The III.24 order would pair him with Egin in the North.
rows.source: Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) II ch. 7 (Scale of Four); cf. III ch. 24; Eng. tr. 1651

rows.name: Orience (Oriens)
rows.role: king of the air, of the East
rows.group: Variant kings — Book of Oberon (Folger V.b.26)
rows.extra: MS c.1577-83. MS p. 73: 'Orience R[ex] of the east'. MS p. 81 section: Oriens reigns in the east; his twelve chief spirits begin with Baall and Agaros. Messenger: Femell / Bellfarto.
rows.note: The manuscript's Office of Spirits opens by naming four kings of the air, with Orience over the East. A later section repeats this and lists twelve principal spirits under him.
rows.source: Folger Shakespeare Library MS V.b.26, 'Officium de spirittibus', MS pp. 73 and 81-82 (transcription by J. H. Peterson and D. Harms, esotericarchives.com/folger; printed as The Book of Oberon, 2015)

rows.name: Paymon
rows.role: king of the air, of the West
rows.group: Variant kings — Book of Oberon (Folger V.b.26)
rows.extra: MS p. 73: 'Paymon R[ex] of the west'. Belferth is called messenger of the king of the west. Beliall heads his twelve (MS p. 83). Agrees with Agrippa.
rows.note: Paymon holds the West in the Oberon set.
rows.source: Folger MS V.b.26, MS pp. 73-74 and 82-83 (Peterson and Harms transcription)

rows.name: Amaymon
rows.role: king of the air, of the South
rows.group: Variant kings — Book of Oberon (Folger V.b.26)
rows.extra: MS p. 73: 'Amaymon R[ex] of the southe'. MS p. 74: the master turns into the South to receive him. His twelve include Asmoday, Bileth and Astaroth (MS p. 82). Agrees with Agrippa.
rows.note: Amaymon holds the South in the Oberon set. The operator is told to face south to receive him, and the text warns that he is very perilous.
rows.source: Folger MS V.b.26, MS pp. 73-74 and 82 (Peterson and Harms transcription)

rows.name: Egine (Egyn, Egin)
rows.role: king of the air, of the North
rows.group: Variant kings — Book of Oberon (Folger V.b.26)
rows.extra: MS p. 73: 'Egine R[ex] of the North'. MS p. 74: look to the North when calling him; 12,000 legions; messengers Rodabell and Lambricon. His twelve end with Annoboth (MS p. 84).
rows.note: Egin holds the North in the Oberon set, and the operator must look north when calling him.
rows.source: Folger MS V.b.26, MS pp. 73-75 and 83-84 (Peterson and Harms transcription)

rows.name: Oriens
rows.role: king of the air, of the East
rows.group: Variant kings — Sloane MS 3853 (Offices of Spirits)
rows.extra: Sloane 3853 fol. 258r. Add. 36674 fol. 65r names Scor, Algor and Sefon as under Oriens, king of the East.
rows.note: This short English offices-of-spirits text names four kings of the air, with Oriens in the East.
rows.source: British Library Sloane MS 3853 fol. 258r, in J. H. Peterson, 'The Offices of Spirits, excerpted from Sloane 3853, Wellcome 110, and Ad. 36674' (esotericarchives.com/solomon/offices.htm)

rows.name: Paymon
rows.role: king of the air, of the West
rows.group: Variant kings — Sloane MS 3853 (Offices of Spirits)
rows.extra: Sloane 3853 fol. 258r
rows.note: Paymon is the king of the West in this list.
rows.source: BL Sloane MS 3853 fol. 258r (Peterson, Offices of Spirits, esotericarchives.com)

rows.name: Amaymon
rows.role: king of the air, of the South
rows.group: Variant kings — Sloane MS 3853 (Offices of Spirits)
rows.extra: Sloane 3853 fol. 258r. Add. 36674 fol. 65r (as 'Amamion') puts Partas and Gamor under him as king of the South.
rows.note: Amaymon is the king of the South in this list.
rows.source: BL Sloane MS 3853 fol. 258r (Peterson, Offices of Spirits, esotericarchives.com)

rows.name: Egim (Egin)
rows.role: king of the air, of the North
rows.group: Variant kings — Sloane MS 3853 (Offices of Spirits)
rows.extra: Sloane 3853 fol. 258r spells 'Egim'. Add. 36674 fol. 65r puts Vmbra and Anaboth under Egin, king of the North.
rows.note: Egim is the king of the North in this list.
rows.source: BL Sloane MS 3853 fol. 258r (Peterson, Offices of Spirits, esotericarchives.com)

rows.name: Oriens
rows.group: Variant kings — Liber 777 (Crowley 1909)
rows.extra: row 11 (Aleph / Air); col. LVII gives '(E) Mezrach' on the same row
rows.note: In 777's Demon Kings column Oriens stands on the Air row, which the Four Quarters column makes East.
rows.source: Crowley, Liber 777 (1909), col. LXVIII 'The Demon Kings' read against col. LVII 'The Four Quarters' (app 777.json)

rows.name: Ariton
rows.group: Variant kings — Liber 777 (Crowley 1909)
rows.extra: row 23 (Mem / Water); col. LVII: '(W) Maareb'. Mathers' 1904 footnote equates Ariton with Egyn, who is North in Agrippa and Oberon.
rows.note: Ariton stands on the Water row, which 777 makes West.
rows.source: Crowley, Liber 777 (1909), cols. LXVIII and LVII (app 777.json)

rows.name: Paimon
rows.group: Variant kings — Liber 777 (Crowley 1909)
rows.extra: row 31 (Shin / Fire); col. LVII: '(S) Darom'
rows.note: Paimon stands on the Fire row, which 777 makes South. This differs from the Goetia's West.
rows.source: Crowley, Liber 777 (1909), cols. LXVIII and LVII (app 777.json)

rows.name: Amaimon
rows.group: Variant kings — Liber 777 (Crowley 1909)
rows.extra: row 32 bis (Earth); col. LVII: '(N) Tzaphon'
rows.note: Amaimon stands on the Earth row, which 777 makes North. This differs from the Goetia's East.
rows.source: Crowley, Liber 777 (1909), cols. LXVIII and LVII (app 777.json)

rows.name: Oriens (Urieus)
rows.role: king of the evil spirits of the East
rows.group: Agrippa — kings of evil spirits of the four parts (cross-reference)
rows.extra: II.7 table: 'Oriens' (row 'Four Princes of spirits, upon the four angles of the world'); III.18: 'Urieus, King of the East'
rows.note: One of four powerful kings Agrippa sets over the evil spirits according to the four parts of the world.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk III ch. 18; Bk II ch. 7

rows.name: Paymon
rows.role: king of the evil spirits of the West
rows.group: Agrippa — kings of evil spirits of the four parts (cross-reference)
rows.extra: cf. goetia.json #9 Paimon, whom the 1904 Goetia says is to be observed towards the West (agrees)
rows.note: Agrippa's King of the West; this agrees with the Goetia's instruction to look West for Paimon.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk III ch. 18; Bk II ch. 7

rows.name: Egyn (Egin)
rows.role: king of the evil spirits of the North
rows.group: Agrippa — kings of evil spirits of the four parts (cross-reference)
rows.extra: II.7: 'Egyn'; III.18: 'Egin, King of the North'
rows.note: Agrippa's King of the North among the four kings of the evil spirits.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk III ch. 18; Bk II ch. 7

rows.name: Amaymon
rows.role: king of the evil spirits of the South
rows.group: Agrippa — kings of evil spirits of the four parts (cross-reference)
rows.extra: CONFLICT: goetia.json #70 Seere (1904 Goetia) calls Amaymon 'King of the East'; Asmoday (#32) and Gaap (#33) are also tied to Amaymon
rows.note: Agrippa's King of the South, while the Goetia puts Amaymon in the East.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk III ch. 18; Bk II ch. 7

rows.name: Samael
rows.group: Agrippa — four princes of devils offensive in the elements (cross-reference)
rows.extra: Heb. סמאל; III.18 spells it 'Samuel', listed first to match Urieus of the East; II.7 puts it in the Fire/East column; both readings agree on East
rows.note: First of the four princes of devils in Agrippa's scale of four, in the Fire/East column; III.18 also pairs this name with the King of the East.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk II ch. 7; Bk III ch. 18

rows.name: Azazel
rows.group: Agrippa — four princes of devils offensive in the elements (cross-reference)
rows.extra: Heb. עזאזל; CONFLICT: II.7 column gives Air/West, but III.18 lists the Hebrew names in the kings' order (East, South, West, North), which would put Azazel in the South
rows.note: One of the four princes of devils in Agrippa's scale of four, in the Air/West column; Agrippa's own ch. 18 ordering implies the South instead.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk II ch. 7; Bk III ch. 18

rows.name: Azael
rows.group: Agrippa — four princes of devils offensive in the elements (cross-reference)
rows.extra: Heb. עזאל; CONFLICT: II.7 column gives Water/North, but the III.18 ordering would put Azael in the West
rows.note: One of the four princes of devils in Agrippa's scale of four, in the Water/North column; Agrippa's own ch. 18 ordering implies the West instead.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk II ch. 7; Bk III ch. 18

rows.name: Mahazael
rows.group: Agrippa — four princes of devils offensive in the elements (cross-reference)
rows.extra: Heb. מהזאל; III.18 spells it 'Mahazuel'; CONFLICT: II.7 column gives Earth/South, but the III.18 ordering would put it in the North
rows.note: One of the four princes of devils in Agrippa's scale of four, in the Earth/South column; Agrippa's own ch. 18 ordering implies the North instead.
rows.source: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy (1651), Bk II ch. 7; Bk III ch. 18

rows.name: Carnesiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Emperors
rows.extra: Sl. 3825 variant: Carnesiell. 1000 great and 100 lesser dukes; 12 chief dukes named. Serves: day and night. Trithemius, Steganographia I.17.
rows.note: Chief emperor ruling in the East. He may appear by day or night with an immense retinue, though far fewer come when only one of his dukes is called.
rows.source: Lemegeton II, Theurgia-Goetia, BL Sloane MS 3825 fol. 118r (J. H. Peterson transcription, esotericarchives.com); cross-check Trithemius, Steganographia (1606) I.17

rows.name: Caspiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Emperors
rows.extra: 200 great and 400 lesser dukes; 12 chief dukes named. Day or night: not stated. Trithemius I.18.
rows.note: Chief emperor ruling in the South. His dukes are described as stubborn and churlish.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 118v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.18

rows.name: Amenadiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Emperors
rows.extra: Trithemius: Armenadiel. 300 great and 500 lesser dukes; 12 named. Serves: any hour of day or night; his dukes take two hours each in turn.
rows.note: Great emperor of the West. He may be called at any hour, while his twelve dukes are called in pairs of hours through the day and night.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 119r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.19

rows.name: Demoriel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Emperors
rows.extra: 400 great and 600 lesser dukes; 12 named, each with 1140 servants. Serves: day and night, his dukes by pairs of hours as for Amenadiel.
rows.note: Great and mighty emperor of the North. His dukes are called by the same hour rule as Amenadiel's.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 119v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.20

rows.name: Pamersiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: Trithemius wind: Oriens (I.1). 11 dukes named. Serves: DAY only. Nature: evil and false.
rows.note: First and chief spirit of the East under Carnesiel. His spirits are called by day with great care; they are false, but good for driving spirits of darkness out of haunted places.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 120r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.1

rows.name: Padiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: MS: 'East and by South'. Trithemius wind: Subsolanus (I.2); Trithemius' figure: Podiel. Azimuth uses the literal 32-point value; on Trithemius' evenly spaced 16-wind rose this slot would be 112.5° (ESE). 10,000 spirits by day and 20,000 by night. Nature: good.
rows.note: Rules as king in the East by South, with ten thousand spirits by day and twenty thousand by night, all good and trustworthy.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 120v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.2

rows.name: Camuel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: Trithemius wind: Eurus (I.3); Trithemius' figure: Cimuel. 10 day and 10 night servants named. Serves: day and night.
rows.note: Rules the south-east part of the world. His servants appear beautiful and courteous; the text says those of the day appear by night and those of the night by day.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 121r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.3

rows.name: Aseliel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: MS: 'South and by East'. Trithemius wind: Euroauster (I.4). Literal 32-point azimuth; the Trithemian 16-wind slot would be 157.5° (SSE). 10 chiefs by day and 20 by night; 8 + 8 named. The spelling 'Aschiel' does not occur in Sl. 3825 or Trithemius.
rows.note: Governs as king under Carnesiel in the South by East. His spirits are courteous, loving and beautiful to see.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 121v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.4

rows.name: Barmiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: Trithemius wind: Auster (I.5). 10 dukes by day and 20 by night; 8 + 8 named. Serves: day and night. Nature: good.
rows.note: First and chief spirit under Caspiel, ruling as king of the South, with dukes for both day and night who obey willingly.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 122r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.5

rows.name: Gediel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: MS: 'South & by West'. Trithemius wind: Austroafricus (I.6). Literal 32-point azimuth; the Trithemian 16-wind slot would be 202.5° (SSW). 20 by day and 20 by night; 8 + 8 named.
rows.note: Rules as king in the South by West, with chief spirits for day and night who are loving and courteous.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 122v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.6

rows.name: Asyriel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: Trithemius: Asiriel, wind Africus (I.7). 20 dukes by day and 20 by night; 8 + 8 named. Day dukes are called by day and night dukes by night.
rows.note: A mighty king of the south-west part of the world. All his dukes are good-natured and willing.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 123r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.7

rows.name: Maseriel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: MS: 'West, and by South'. Trithemius wind: Favonius (I.8). Literal 32-point azimuth; the Trithemian 16-wind slot would be 247.5° (WSW). 12 by day and 12 by night named, each with 30 servants.
rows.note: Rules as king in the dominion of the West by South. His spirits are good by nature; those of the day are called by day and those of the night by night.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 123v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.8

rows.name: Malgaras
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: Trithemius wind: Occidens (I.9). 30 dukes by day and 30 by night; 12 + 12 named. Serves: day and night.
rows.note: First under the emperor of the West, ruling as king in the West. His courteous dukes appear two by two with their servants.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 124r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.9

rows.name: Dorochiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: MS: 'West, and by North'. Trithemius: Dorothiel, wind Chorus (I.10). Literal 32-point azimuth; the Trithemian 16-wind slot would be 292.5° (WNW). 40 by day and 40 by night; 24 + 24 named, called by planetary hours.
rows.note: A mighty prince ruling in the West by North. His good-natured dukes are called two per planetary hour through the day and night.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 124v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.10

rows.name: Usiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: Trithemius: Vsiel, wind Subcircius (I.11). 40 diurnal and 40 nocturnal dukes; 14 + 14 named.
rows.note: A mighty prince ruling as king in the north-west. His dukes are said to have more power than any others to hide or reveal treasure.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 125v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.11

rows.name: Cabariel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: The Sl. 3825 heading gives no point. Sl. 2731 adds 'West & by North', which would duplicate Dorochiel. The conjuration says 'North & by West', and Trithemius' Circius (I.12) lies between Subcircius (NW) and Septentrio (N). Literal 32-point azimuth; the Trithemian 16-wind slot would be 337.5° (NNW). 50 by day (good) and 50 by night (evil).
rows.note: His conjuration places him as king in the North by West. His day dukes are good and obedient; his night dukes are evil and deceitful.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 126v, conjuration (Peterson transcription, with Sl. 2731 variant); Trithemius, Steganographia I.12

rows.name: Raysiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: Trithemius wind: Septentrio (I.13). 50 by day and 50 by night; 16 day (good) and 14 night (evil) named.
rows.note: First under the emperor of the North, ruling as king in the North. His day dukes are good and his night dukes evil and stubborn.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 127r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.13

rows.name: Symiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: MS: 'North & by Easte'. Trithemius wind: Aquilo (I.14). Literal 32-point azimuth; the Trithemian 16-wind slot would be 22.5° (NNE). 10 by day and 1000 by night; 10 + 10 named.
rows.note: Rules as king in the North by East. His day dukes are good, while his night dukes are stubborn and unwilling.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 127v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.14

rows.name: Armadiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: Trithemius wind: Boreas (I.15). 15 chief dukes with 1260 servants each. Serves: day and night, divided into 15 parts from sunrise.
rows.note: Rules as king in the north-east part. His good dukes are called in turn through the day and night, which is divided into fifteen parts.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 128r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.15

rows.name: Baruchas
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Kings of the compass points
rows.extra: MS: 'East and by North'. Trithemius wind: Vulturnus (I.16). Literal 32-point azimuth; the Trithemian 16-wind slot would be 67.5° (ENE). 15 chief dukes, 7040 servants. Serves: day and night in 15 parts.
rows.note: Rules as king in the East by North. His dukes are good and are called through the day and night in fifteen parts, as with Armadiel.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 128v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.16

rows.name: Geradiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
rows.extra: Sl. 3825 also spells it Garadiel. No dukes; 18,150 servants. Serves: day and night, with the number of servants varying by planetary hour. Trithemius I.21.
rows.note: First of the eleven princes who wander the air with no fixed place, so the facing direction does not matter. He is called alone, and more or fewer servants come depending on the hour.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 129r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.21

rows.name: Buriel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
rows.extra: 12 dukes (one per night hour), 880 servants each. Serves: NIGHT only. Nature: evil. Trithemius I.22.
rows.note: His spirits are evil, hated by all other spirits, and hate the day, so they are called only at night. They appear as serpents with a maiden's head.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 129v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.22

rows.name: Hydriel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
rows.extra: 100 great and 200 lesser dukes; 12 named. Serves: day and night by planetary hours. Trithemius I.23.
rows.note: His courteous dukes come by day or night as serpents with maidens' heads, and they delight in waters and moist ground.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 130r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.23

rows.name: Pirichiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
rows.extra: Trithemius: Pyrichiel (I.24). Knights instead of dukes: 8 named, 2000 servants. Called according to planetary motion; day or night is not specified.
rows.note: A wandering prince who has knights instead of dukes, all good by nature.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 130v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.24

rows.name: Emoniel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
rows.extra: 100 princes and dukes plus 20 under-dukes; 12 named. Serves: day and night in planetary order. Trithemius I.25.
rows.note: A good-natured wandering prince whose dukes come willingly by day or night and mostly dwell in woods.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 131r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.25

rows.name: Icosiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
rows.extra: 100 dukes and 300 companions; 15 named, 2200 servants. Serves: day and night, the 24 hours divided into 15 parts from sunrise.
rows.note: His good-natured dukes most often appear in houses.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 131v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.26

rows.name: Soleviel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
rows.extra: Trithemius: Soleuiel (I.27). 200 dukes and 200 companions; 12 named, 1840 servants. Serves: day and night by planetary hours.
rows.note: A wandering prince whose dukes and companions change places every year; all are good and obedient.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 132r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.27

rows.name: Menadiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
rows.extra: Trithemius I.28 (printed 'Menachiel'). 20 dukes and 100 companions; 6 + 6 named, 390 servants. Called according to planetary motion, alternating a duke and a companion.
rows.note: A good, obedient wandering prince. A duke and then a companion are called in successive planetary hours.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 132v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.28

rows.name: Macariel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
rows.extra: 12 chief dukes named, 400 servants. Serves: day and night in planetary order.
rows.note: A wandering prince whose dukes are good by nature and obedient to the exorcist.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 133r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.29

rows.name: Uriel (Theurgia)
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
rows.extra: Not the archangel. 10 chief and 100 lesser dukes; 10 named, 650 servants. Day or night: not stated. Nature: evil.
rows.note: A wandering prince whose dukes are evil, unwilling and false, and appear as serpents with maidens' heads.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 133v (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.30

rows.name: Bidiel
rows.group: Theurgia-Goetia — Wandering princes
rows.extra: Trithemius: Bydiel (I.31). 20 dukes and 200 lesser dukes; 10 named, 2400 servants. Day or night: not stated.
rows.note: The last wandering prince. His good dukes change office and place every year and appear in beautiful human form.
rows.source: Theurgia-Goetia, Sloane MS 3825 fol. 134r (Peterson transcription); Trithemius, Steganographia I.31

rows.name: Varcan
rows.group: Heptameron — kings of the air
rows.extra: Ministers: Tus, Andas, Cynabal. Latin wind: Boreas (also in Folger V.b.26: 'subditi Boreae'), which Turner renders 'North-winde'.
rows.note: King of the aerial spirits of Sunday, under the North wind. His spirits bring gold, gems, riches, favour and honours.
rows.source: Heptameron (attrib. Peter de Abano), Considerations of Sunday; Eng. R. Turner in The Fourth Book of Occult Philosophy (1655; B. Rowe transcription)

rows.name: Arcan
rows.group: Heptameron — kings of the air
rows.extra: Ministers: Bilet, Missabu, Abuzaha. Latin wind: Zephyrus, 'the wind of the Moon'.
rows.note: King of Monday's aerial spirits, under the West wind, which the text calls the wind of the Moon. They give silver, carry things from place to place and reveal secrets.
rows.source: Heptameron (Turner 1655), Considerations of Monday

rows.name: Samax
rows.group: Heptameron — kings of the air
rows.extra: Ministers: Carmax, Ismoli, Paffran. Latin wind: Subsolanus.

rows.extra: Liber Chanokh: BATAIVAH, 'great King of the East'; tablet names ORO IBAH AOZPI; every reading of Dee's own material also puts the ORO tablet in the East (agrees)
rows.note: The king-name read in a whorl around the centre of the Air tablet, which the Golden Dawn and Liber Chanokh put in the East.
rows.source: Crowley, Liber Chanokh (Liber LXXXIV), The Equinox I:7–8 (1912): explanation of the tablets, Plate IV 'The Great Watch-Tower of the East, attributed to Air', and the tablet invocations (from Golden Dawn Enochian papers)

rows.name: Edlprnaa
rows.role: Great King of the Fire Watchtower
rows.group: Enochian Watchtower Kings (Golden Dawn attribution)
rows.extra: Liber Chanokh prints EDLPRNAA; its invocation gives the spoken form EDELPERNA ('great King of the South'); tablet OIP TEAA PDOCE; DISPUTED for Dee: OIP in the North per enochian.blog (12 Dec 2025), in the West per enochian.blog (20 Jan 2026) and Stenwick (2014, Tabula Recensa)
rows.note: King of the Fire tablet, which the Golden Dawn puts in the South; modern readings of Dee's own records put this tablet elsewhere.
rows.source: Liber Chanokh (Equinox I:7–8, 1912), explanation of the tablets, Plate VII 'The Great Watch-Tower of the South, attributed to Fire' and invocation; Dee readings per enochian.blog and Augoeides blog (Stenwick)

rows.name: Raagiosl
rows.role: Great King of the Water Watchtower
rows.group: Enochian Watchtower Kings (Golden Dawn attribution)
rows.extra: Liber Chanokh prints RAAGIOSL; its invocation gives the spoken form RAAGIOSEL ('great King of the West'); tablet MPH ARSL GAIOL; DISPUTED for Dee: MPH in the West per enochian.blog (12 Dec 2025, agrees), in the South per enochian.blog (20 Jan 2026) and Stenwick (2014, Tabula Recensa)
rows.note: King of the Water tablet, which the Golden Dawn puts in the West.
rows.source: Liber Chanokh (Equinox I:7–8, 1912), explanation of the tablets, Plate V 'The Great Watch-Tower of the West, attributed to Water' and invocation; Dee readings per enochian.blog and Augoeides blog (Stenwick)

rows.name: Iczhhcal
rows.role: Great King of the Earth Watchtower
rows.group: Enochian Watchtower Kings (Golden Dawn attribution)
rows.extra: Liber Chanokh prints ICZHHCAL; its invocation gives the spoken form IC-ZOD-HEH-CAL ('great King of the North'); common GD variant ICZHIHAL; tablet MOR DIAL HCTGA; DISPUTED for Dee: MOR in the South per enochian.blog (12 Dec 2025), in the North per enochian.blog (20 Jan 2026) and Stenwick (2014, Tabula Recensa; agrees)
rows.note: King of the Earth tablet, which the Golden Dawn puts in the North; one modern reading of Dee's records puts this tablet in the South.
rows.source: Liber Chanokh (Equinox I:7–8, 1912), explanation of the tablets, Plate VI 'The Great Watch-Tower of the North, attributed to Earth' and invocation; Dee readings per enochian.blog and Augoeides blog (Stenwick)
